learning_outcomes.text: Acquire and utilize fundamental chemistry notions necessary to understand the properties, composition, and behavior of various categories of substances and materials, and the correlations between substance structure and their physical and mechanical properties.
Define basic notions, concepts, theories, and models in chemistry applicable to mechanical engineering.
Utilize basic knowledge from fundamental sciences to explain and interpret engineering phenomena.
Identify and apply concepts, methods, and theories to solve engineering problems with qualified assistance.
Critically analyze and utilize principles, methods, and working techniques for quantitative and qualitative evaluation of processes.
Provide theoretical grounding for solving domain-specific problems using established principles and methods.
Utilize basic knowledge from fundamental sciences to explain and interpret corrosion processes and anticorrosive protection.
Critically analyze and utilize principles, methods, and working techniques for quantitative and qualitative evaluation of corrosion processes.
Describe basic concepts, theories, and methods of anticorrosive protection.
Explain and interpret principles and methods used in the anticorrosive protection of industrial installations.
Utilize acquired knowledge to explain and interpret various concepts and processes encountered in mechanical engineering.
Define basic notions, concepts, theories, and models in the field of metal and alloy corrosion.
Identify and apply concepts, methods, and theories to solve corrosion and anticorrosive protection problems.

syllabus_topics: Correlations between substance structure and properties: Atomic structure of substances, electronic shell structure, chemical bonds
Laws of gases: Law of isothermal transformations, law of isobaric transformations, law of isochoric transformations, ideal gas state equation
Chemical reactions: Classification of chemical reactions, Stoichiometry, Stoichiometric calculations
Industrial water: Classification of waters, quality conditions imposed on waters, purification of natural waters
Fuels: Classification of fuels, obtaining, composition, characterization, and uses
Notions of electrochemistry, corrosion, and anticorrosive protection: Corrosion, Protection against corrosion
Determination of physicochemical characteristics of materials
Preparation of solutions of various concentrations
Determination of water hardness, water softening
Determination of viscosity index for lubricating oils
Determination of penetration for consistent greases
Determination of cetane number for diesel fuels

assessment_methods.method: Practical activities (involvement, results presentation, interpretation, lab reports, tests)

assessment_rules: A minimum grade of 5 must be obtained for both written assignments corresponding to the distributed evaluation. The ongoing activity can be concluded with a minimum grade of 5, provided all laboratory work is completed and all associated reports are submitted.
